situation.text: Norway signed for 70 CV90 infantry fighting vehicles worth just over NOK 20 bn in Stockholm on 27 November, as part of a five-nation order, with large orders promised to Norwegian subcontractors. Ukraine's former commander-in-chief Syrskyi toured the Russian border with Norway's defence chief this week to help strengthen air defences against drones and missiles. A sanctioned Russian ship that has carried weapons for Russia's defence ministry is docked in Svalbard.

Sweden, Finland, Norway, Lithuania and the Netherlands signed the SEK 60 bn CV90 order on 27 November, the largest in BAE Systems Hägglunds' history, and it includes counter-drone systems shaped by Ukraine. Estonia closes its land border with Russia on 1 December, citing sabotage. Finnish police are investigating suspected drone spying on Nammo's powder plant.

Russia launched 162 drones overnight on 28 November and struck Kharkiv with missiles, after an attack on Nizhyn that killed seven. Ukraine hit the Novoshakhtinsk refinery and a Samara oil pumping station for the second time this week. Cheap interceptor drones are now a main tool against Shaheds: one maker says its Bullet downed 1,200 in a month.

The EU is preparing tens of billions of euros in loans and grants, from the second half of 2027, to cut Europe's reliance on the US for intelligence, air defence and logistics. Poland has asked NATO to consider shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine that head for allied territory. The UK is moving money from Storm Shadow to cheap mass-produced munitions.

news.title: Norway signs for 70 CV90s worth NOK 20 bn
news.summary: FMA signed the contract in Stockholm for 70 CV9035 MkIV Nordic Edition vehicles, with an option for four more, as part of the five-nation order led by Sweden. Deliveries are planned for 2030–2034 to Brigade Nord and Finnmark Brigade. The value of just over NOK 20 bn includes spares, ammunition and training material, plus rebuilding some older CV90s and buying 120 mm mortars. BAE Systems Hägglunds will place large orders with Norwegian subcontractors, and the vehicles get protection against drones and an active protection system.

news.title: Sanctioned Russian weapons-transport ship docks in Svalbard
news.summary: A Barents Observer investigation shows the Tambey, now docked in Barentsburg, has repeatedly carried military cargo, including weapons, for Russia's defence ministry in the Arctic. Russia has protested Norway's seizure of another ship, the Professor Molchanov, held in Barentsburg on a claim by Naftogaz.

news.title: Norway's Gardar leads two USD 5 m defence rounds in a week
news.summary: The Norwegian fund led rounds in drone-detection startup Pai Defence and Ukrainian military communications maker HIMERA, which each raised USD 5 m. Gardar is one of the most active Norwegian investors in Ukrainian defence tech.

news.title: Fjord Defence Group's revenue jumps ninefold
news.summary: The Oslo-listed group has closed its largest acquisition so far, the Swedish defence manufacturer PartnerTech. It reports an order backlog of NOK 1.7 bn. Norwegian defence suppliers are growing through buying up Nordic subcontractors.

news.title: Syrskyi helps Norway plan air defence on the Russian border
news.summary: Ukraine's former commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi toured the 198 km border with Russia with Norway's Chief of Defence Eirik Kristoffersen. The aim is to strengthen air defences against drones and missiles. Syrskyi said Norway should be ready for provocations and keep air defences on standby around the clock.

news.title: Ukraine: Norway sets aside USD 7 bn in military aid for 2027
news.summary: Ukraine's defence ministry says Norway will give USD 7 bn in military aid in 2027, the same as in 2026, and is the largest contributor to NATO's PURL scheme that buys Patriot missiles. Kyiv wants most of the 2027 money to go to drones, with air defence, aviation and electronic warfare as other priorities. Norway also supplies automated turrets against jet-powered Shaheds and is developing interceptors with Ukraine.

news.title: Maritime Robotics targets fivefold growth by 2030
news.summary: The Norwegian uncrewed vessel maker had revenue of NOK 258.8 m in 2025 and aims for five times that in 2030. The CEO says selling to Norway's own armed forces remains a big challenge.

news.title: FMA seeks NOK 500 m deal to keep Bell 412 helicopters flying
news.summary: FMA has opened a competition for engine maintenance, spare parts and support for the Bell 412's PT6T engines, valued at NOK 500 m. With options the contract could run for 17 years. Replacement helicopters are not due to be bought before 2030. Qualification deadline is 6 January 2027.

news.title: Clavister to supply cyber protection for the new CV90s
news.summary: Swedish cybersecurity company Clavister will supply its CyberArmour for the vehicles in the five-nation CV90 deal, with deliveries from 2028. Hägglunds says the order will spread work across scores of subcontractors and includes counter-drone systems shaped by the war in Ukraine.

news.title: FMV orders twelve more Gavia underwater drones
news.summary: Sweden's procurement agency FMV has taken over last year's Teledyne Gavia autonomous underwater vehicles and ordered twelve more for delivery in 2027 and 2028.

news.title: STARK's sea drone production in Denmark is delayed
news.summary: STARK and Seasight Solutions planned to start building Vanta uncrewed surface vessels in Ringkøbing in October. Nearly two months later no vessels have been built in Denmark.

news.title: Finland confirms 160 CV90s for EUR 1.96 bn
news.summary: Finland will buy 160 CV9035 Mk IV Nordic Edition vehicles with an option for 100 more, as part of the five-nation buy. Finnish companies get more than 30% of the value, and part is financed with EU SAFE loans. The minister says the vehicles will also be able to counter drones.

news.title: Danish armed forces seek 20 suppliers for DKK 5.6 bn security deal
news.summary: The framework covers alarms, access control and physical protection at military sites. Companies can learn more at an information meeting on 1 December.

news.title: Denmark to let domestic firms test uncrewed maritime tech with the military
news.summary: Companies from Denmark, Greenland and the Faroe Islands can apply from the end of 2026 to test their systems with the Danish armed forces in 2027.

news.title: Estonia to close its last rail crossing with Russia over sabotage
news.summary: Estonia plans to close the Narva railway crossing, its last rail link to Russia. The prime minister cites continued hostile activity and numerous incidents on Estonian territory.

news.title: Finland investigates suspected drone spying on Nammo powder plant
news.summary: Finland's National Bureau of Investigation is looking into drone flights over Nammo's Vihtavuori gunpowder factory in Laukaa between 1 and 5 September. There are no suspects. The plant makes powder for small-arms and artillery ammunition and got EUR 10 m from the EU in 2024 to grow capacity.

news.title: Ukraine hits Novoshakhtinsk refinery and Samara oil station again
news.summary: Ukrainian drones struck the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Rostov region and an oil pumping station in Samara region overnight, starting fires at both. It was the second strike on these sites this week.

news.title: Bullet interceptor drones downed 1,200 Shaheds in a month
news.summary: Maker General Cherry says its Bullet interceptors destroyed 1,200 Shahed-type drones in the past month. Their share of Shahed interceptions rose from about 15% in September to about 37% in November. Units bought them with ePoints on the Brave1 Market.

news.title: Ukraine now makes over half its own artillery shells
news.summary: Rheinmetall's CEO says Ukrainian production covers more than half of the 1 to 1.3 million shells Ukraine uses a year. Ukrainian officers still report an acute shortage of ammunition.

news.title: Drones strike St Petersburg and the Leningrad region
news.summary: Explosions were reported in at least eight districts of St Petersburg overnight, and video appears to show a hit on a power substation. The regional governor claims 45 drones were shot down. Pulkovo airport was temporarily restricted.

news.title: Zelensky warns Russia is preparing a new large-scale attack
news.summary: President Zelensky told Ukrainians to watch missile alerts in the coming days. He says Ukraine is working with partners in Europe and beyond on extra arms packages to protect infrastructure, especially against drones.

news.title: Ukraine opens DELTA to Norway and Germany, AI test lab to UK and Denmark
news.summary: At NATO Edge 26, Ukraine said Germany and Norway have agreements on access to its DELTA battle management system. The UK and Denmark are the first foreign partners in Avengers Labs, where companies train and test AI models on more than five million annotated combat frames without taking the data out. Brave1 also showed Brave1 Market, a catalogue of over 5,000 technologies units can buy from directly.

news.title: Tryzub-3000 laser enters combat use
news.summary: The first Ukrainian unit has begun training on and deploying the 3 kW Tryzub-3000 laser from Celebra Tech, cleared for combat use in September. It uses AI-based guidance linked to radars and can run automatically or semi-autonomously against FPV drones and munitions.

news.title: Ballistic missiles hit Kyiv industrial area and a shopping mall
news.summary: Russia attacked Kyiv with ballistic missiles on the evening of 25 November. Buildings in an industrial area of the Desnianskyi district and a shopping mall were hit, and at least one person was hospitalised.

news.title: EU prepares new defence loans to cut reliance on the US
news.summary: The EU is preparing loans and grants worth tens of billions of euros to help countries build intelligence, surveillance, air and missile defence and logistics they now get from the US. The programme is expected to start in the second half of 2027, and the amount is not set.

news.title: EU plans EUR 50 bn fund for tech sovereignty
news.summary: The fund could be run by an independent investment firm, like the EU-backed vehicle that co-led ICEYE's EUR 1 bn round this summer.

news.title: UK moves Storm Shadow money to cheap mass-produced munitions
news.summary: A senior UK officer told Parliament's Defence Committee that money set aside for new Storm Shadow missiles now goes to low-cost munitions like those used in Ukraine, made in the UK. He said too much of the budget went to complex, expensive weapons.

news.title: Proposed EU budget cuts money for defence industry and space
news.summary: European Council President Costa's proposal for the 2028–2034 EU budget lowers funding for the defence industry and space. A Swedish researcher expects the final figure to be lower still.

news.title: Poland asks NATO to consider shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine
news.summary: Poland raised the idea at a meeting of NATO ambassadors in Brussels, for missiles heading towards NATO countries. Some allies supported it, but talks were preliminary and any decision needs unanimity. NATO will deploy an AWACS aircraft to monitor Polish airspace.

news.title: Germany to form its first drone regiment
news.summary: Internal documents reported by POLITICO show the Bundeswehr's first drone regiment will have reconnaissance drones, jamming systems, interceptor drones and long-range strike systems, much of it Ukrainian-made. Forming starts in 2027 with about 350 troops, growing to about 600 by 2029.

news.title: ARX's ground robot joins British Army targeting network
news.summary: German ARX Robotics says its GEREON was the first ground robot connected to the British Army's ASGARD targeting network, during an exercise in Kenya. The Army says the time from detecting a target to acting fell to a tenth. 4 Brigade deploys to NATO's eastern flank in April 2027.

news.title: STARK and Helsing loitering munitions pass German live-fire trials
news.summary: Germany's defence ministry says STARK's VIRTUS and Helsing's HX-2 passed live-fire trials in November, meeting a key requirement for training. Full qualification is still under way. First deliveries to the Bundeswehr are expected by the end of 2026.

press.titleNo: Norge kjøper nye kampvogner til Hæren
press.title: Norway buys new infantry fighting vehicles for the Army
press.summary: Norway, Sweden, Finland, the Netherlands and Lithuania signed contracts for the same CV90 vehicle in Stockholm on 27 November. FMA is buying 70 CV9035 MkIV Nordic Edition vehicles, with an option for four more, for delivery in 2030–2034 to Brigade Nord and Finnmark Brigade. The value is just over NOK 20 bn including spares, special tools, ammunition and training material; the project also rebuilds some older CV90s and buys 120 mm mortars. BAE Systems Hägglunds will place large orders with Norwegian subcontractors. The vehicles are protected against drone attacks and get an automatic protection system against incoming drones and missiles.
press.startup: Large orders will flow to Norwegian subcontractors over 2027–2034. Inference: makers of counter-drone, sensor, cyber and digital vehicle systems should approach Hägglunds' supply chain and its Norwegian partners now.
press.tldr: NOK 20 bn CV90 deal opens Norwegian subcontracting work into the 2030s.

press.titleNo: Fakta om rammeavtaler i Forsvaret: Dette gjør vi
press.title: Facts about framework agreements in Forsvaret: what we are doing
press.summary: Forsvaret says missing framework agreements cause problems for units, and the Office of the Auditor General has confirmed weaknesses in how agreements are followed up. Causes include limited capacity, trouble recruiting procurement staff and poor digital tools. Forsvaret has created local purchasing units and raised local purchasing limits. FMA and Forsvaret will move to fewer, broader agreements with longer terms, and FMA and Forsvarsbygg are now responsible for signing framework agreements.
press.startup: Inference: fewer, larger and longer framework agreements make it harder to get in as a small supplier, so partnering with a prime or bidding through dynamic purchasing systems matters more. Higher local purchasing limits may help small direct sales to units.
press.tldr: Fewer, bigger framework deals ahead: partner up or use dynamic purchasing systems.

press.title: Strengthening Norwegian-Ukrainian security cooperation
press.summary: Ukraine's defence minister Yevhenii Khmara visited Defence Minister Tore O. Sandvik in Oslo on 24 November. They discussed expanding DESNA, an air defence system developed by Kongsberg and a Ukrainian partner, in which cheap Ukrainian-made missiles and launchers are linked to Norwegian-donated Kongsberg fire control. Norway has bought and donated several DESNA systems in recent months, and they already protect Ukraine against drones. The government is working to expand the project to cover larger areas. The ministers also signed a letter of intent that lets Forsvaret test Delta, Ukraine's data platform for situational awareness and battle management, with no exchange of operational data.
press.startup: Norway is now paying to combine cheap Ukrainian hardware with Norwegian systems, and wants to learn from Ukrainian software. Inference: Norwegian–Ukrainian teams that integrate with Kongsberg or feed data into C2 platforms like Delta have a clear buyer story.
press.tldr: Cheap Ukrainian tech plus Norwegian integration is what Norway now funds.

press.titleNo: FMA gjennomfører nasjonal konkurranse om bygging av standardiserte fartøy
press.title: FMA runs a national competition to build the standardised vessels
press.summary: FMA says interest in the standardised vessels is high and it will run a national competition among Norwegian suppliers. The buy is split into two contracts and financial security requirements are reduced, so more yards can compete. Key figures such as equity are not absolute minimums, and yards can meet them through joint bids or a supporting company. Hulls may be built in Norway, but there is no general requirement for it. Prequalification is now under way.
press.startup: Two contracts and joint bids mean more yards in play, and each will need subsuppliers for sensors, autonomy and onboard systems. Talk to the yards that prequalify now (inference).
press.tldr: Navy ship race stays Norwegian; pitch onboard tech to the bidding yards.

press.titleNo: Tester dronekrig under øvelse Viking Ymer
press.title: Testing drone warfare in exercise Viking Ymer
press.summary: The Army's battalion exercise Viking Ymer was used to test how infantry and manoeuvre units can operate on a battlefield full of drones. Several exercise goals answer research questions, tying the exercise closely to FFI. The head of the Drone School says moving supplies forward by truck is now very hard, and a driverless tracked vehicle linked to a radar and remotely controlled was tested. The Army says it watches Ukraine and translates what it learns to Norwegian terrain and climate.
press.startup: The Army is openly looking for ways to resupply and evacuate without exposing soldiers, and runs exercises with FFI research goals. Inference: UGV, autonomy and counter-detection startups should ask FFI and the Army Weapons School about joining the next exercise.
press.tldr: The Army wants uncrewed resupply; exercises with FFI are the way in.

press.title: Government to invest in air defence missiles
press.summary: The revised 2026 defence budget proposes buying air defence missiles for about NOK 22 bn, with a P85 cost frame of NOK 21,257 m. The missiles are AIM-9X, AMRAAM 120C and AMRAAM Extended Range, all for NASAMS ground launchers. They will protect Ørland, Evenes, critical infrastructure, allied reception areas and Army forces against drones, aircraft and helicopters. The aim is to replace old missiles, replace those donated to Ukraine and build larger stocks. The minister says stocks also deter.
press.startup: The money goes to US missiles and Kongsberg, not to startups. The opening is around it: sensors, C2, cheap effectors and drone detection that let costly missiles be saved for the right targets (inference).
press.tldr: Big missile money goes to primes; sell what makes each missile count.

press.titleNo: Hæren kan ikke vinne kampen alene
press.title: The Army cannot win the fight alone
press.summary: On 17 November more than 150 people from Forsvaret, municipalities, business and emergency services met in Elverum to discuss the Army's endurance in war. The Chief of the Army said Forsvaret loses fighting power if it must spend resources keeping society running. Business leaders asked the Army to involve industry earlier in its planning, since much of the capacity it needs sits in private firms. One transport CEO said the next step is to move from goodwill to concrete agreements.
press.startup: The Army is opening up to firm agreements with private suppliers for wartime support. Logistics, communications and resilience startups should get into these planning talks early (inference).
press.tldr: Total defence is shifting to contracts; get into the Army's planning early.

press.title: Atlantic Future Forum 2026: co-hosts' statement
press.summary: Representatives of 29 countries met in Oslo on 11–12 November aboard HMS Prince of Wales, at the invitation of the UK and Norway. They affirmed NATO as the base of collective security and welcomed greater European leadership in deterrence and defence. They noted the Northern Navies Framework signed by Joint Expeditionary Force naval chiefs on 10 November. The statement backs continued support for Ukraine and whole-of-society resilience. It calls for more production, faster technological innovation and a stronger European defence industrial base, including start-ups and SMEs alongside established primes.
press.startup: A political signal, not a programme: no money or procurement is attached. It gives startups a quotable line when they ask Norwegian and British buyers for a place next to the primes (inference).
press.tldr: Norway and the UK say start-ups belong next to the primes; hold them to it.

press.title: The industry portal for Ukraine has changed
press.summary: The portal, set up in November 2024 for Norwegian offers of technology and materiel to Ukraine, is now a marketplace showing defence capacities and opportunities. Ukraine's defence ministry should as a rule verify that a product matches a Ukrainian need. The portal no longer gets annual earmarked Nansen funds; unused money moves to the ordinary military support budget. FMA assesses the commercial, technical and legal side of proposals that match confirmed needs, and Forsvaret decides based on Ukrainian priorities and the budget. A ministry review found the old setup lacked clear rules for handling cases.
press.startup: Registering an offer no longer means a funded project; buys happen only when Ukraine confirms a concrete need. Startups should register and also build direct contact with Ukrainian units and Brave1 to get needs confirmed (inference).
press.tldr: Register on the portal, but get Ukraine to confirm the need first.

press.title: Work begins on a Nordic defence agreement
press.summary: Norway, Denmark, Finland, Sweden and Iceland will start work on a Nordic defence agreement, agreed at the NORDEFCO ministers' meeting in Oslo on 11–12 November. The goal is closer cooperation that strengthens NATO deterrence and lets Nordic forces operate seamlessly across borders. Ministers discussed a legal and political framework for peace, crisis and war, and want to remove practical and legal obstacles to moving forces. The Nordic countries together have about 250 modern fighter jets, 145 surface vessels and 100,000 personnel in peacetime. No timeline was given.
press.startup: The release does not mention procurement, but common rules for moving forces point toward more shared exercises, logistics and systems (inference). Products that work across all Nordic forces will have a bigger market.
press.tldr: Nordic forces are integrating; sell to all five, not one.

press.title: MoD asks agencies to prepare corrective actions after audit
press.summary: Riksrevisjonen found that the 2025 accounts of Forsvaret, FFI and FMA may contain material errors, and could not give an opinion on Forsvarsbygg. The MoD has ordered concrete action plans with reporting requirements. Forsvaret must strengthen inventory control with an annual stock-count plan, FMA risks booking purchases in the wrong fiscal year, and Forsvarsbygg gets an external review of its financial management.
press.startup: Expect stricter documentation on deliveries, invoice timing and inventory traceability when you sell to FMA or Forsvaret. There may be demand for inventory, traceability and financial-control tools.
press.tldr: Expect stricter paperwork when you deliver to FMA and Forsvaret.

press.title: Forsvaret modernises its emergency-network radios
press.summary: Forsvaret will buy 1,320 new terminals for Nødnett, the radio network shared with police, fire and health services. About 650 replace first-generation equipment; the Army gets 280 and the Home Guard 290. The new handheld Motorola MXP600 replaces the MT P850S, delivered through TC Connect and funded through the Defence Staff's ICT portfolio. Forsvaret says it needs several ways to communicate, including robust ground systems alongside satellite and broadband, and that the upgrade also eases cooperation with Nordic emergency services.
press.startup: The contract is already placed, so there is nothing to bid on. It shows Forsvaret values redundant communications and civil-military interoperability in total defence, a theme comms and C2 startups can pitch to (inference).
press.tldr: No tender, but Forsvaret wants redundant comms that work with civilian services.

readings.title: The “Battle of Norway”
readings.publisher: Sahaidachnyi Security Center, supported by Buntar Aerospace
readings.summary: Argues that the most likely attack on Norway is not a ground invasion of Finnmark but a 'Battle of Britain' in the drone era: mass drone and missile strikes, sea drones and sabotage against energy, subsea cables and logistics. It sees a threat window of 2027–2029, while most Norwegian programmes mature in 2029–2036. Biggest gaps: counter-drone and ballistic defence, sabotage detection at sea, tactical electronic warfare and manpower in Finnmark. Recommends a standing Ukraine–Norway capability partnership, starting with a Home Guard counter-drone shield.
readings.tldr: Norway's real gap is cheap mass defence against drones and sabotage, and Ukraine can help close it fast.

readings.title: Sabotage threat in Norway raised
readings.summary: PST's updated assessment says Russian intelligence will likely attempt sabotage in Norway in the coming year, mostly through proxies. The defence industry, defence-related businesses and their suppliers are the most likely targets, followed by critical infrastructure such as energy. PST asks companies to know their normal picture and report anything that deviates from it.
readings.tldr: Defence startups and their suppliers are now named sabotage targets; secure your sites.

readings.title: EU strategy for a rapidly changing Arctic
readings.summary: The EU's new Arctic strategy replaces the 2021 framework and puts security and resilience first. It plans a maritime security hub for sharing information and monitoring Arctic waters, more icebreaker capacity and protection of critical infrastructure such as a secure subsea cable to Greenland. Russia's military build-up and hybrid tactics in the north are the stated reason.
readings.tldr: EU money and attention are moving to Arctic surveillance and infrastructure protection.

readings.title: National Threat Assessment 2026
readings.summary: Russian and Chinese intelligence activity is expected to rise, with focus on military targets, Ukraine support, the High North and critical infrastructure. Essential context for anyone selling security or surveillance tech.
readings.tldr: Russian and Chinese spying in Norway is rising; expect stricter security demands on suppliers.

readings.title: Fokus 2026
readings.summary: The intelligence service's annual open assessment of the external threats to Norway, with Russia's military posture in the north at the centre.
readings.tldr: Russia's military power in the north remains the core threat to Norway.

readings.title: Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014–2026)
readings.summary: Official spending, share of GDP, equipment share and personnel for all allies. The numbers on the map above come from here.
readings.tldr: Every ally but Slovenia now spends 2%+ of GDP; the money is there.

readings.title: Forsvarsløftet: long-term plan for the defence sector 2025–2036
readings.summary: The cross-party plan behind about NOK 600 bn in extra defence spending over 12 years. Tells you what Norway will buy and when.
readings.tldr: NOK 600 bn extra over 12 years: this is Norway's shopping list.

readings.title: Meld. St. 33 (2024–2025): status of the long-term plan
readings.summary: Progress, challenges and risks in delivering the long-term plan. Useful to see where programmes are late and where faster solutions are needed.
readings.tldr: Several programmes are late; that is where faster solutions are welcome.

readings.title: Roadmap for increased production capacity in the defence industry
readings.summary: The government's roadmap for scaling Norwegian defence production. Relevant for manufacturers and suppliers to the primes.
readings.tldr: Norway wants more production at home; manufacturers and subsuppliers benefit.

readings.title: New law on defence and security procurement (report)
readings.summary: Proposal for a new procurement law for defence and security. Shapes how startups can be bought from in the future.
readings.tldr: Procurement rules are being rewritten; watch how they treat small firms.

readings.title: National Security Strategy
readings.summary: Norway's first national security strategy, tying together defence, total defence, economy and technology.
readings.tldr: Security now spans defence, economy and technology, which widens the dual-use market.

readings.title: Readiness Roadmap 2030
readings.summary: The EU's four flagships, including the European Drone Defence Initiative and Eastern Flank Watch, with milestones to 2030.
readings.tldr: The EU wants a working drone shield and eastern flank watch by 2027–2030.

readings.title: White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030
readings.summary: The ReArm Europe plan, up to EUR 800 bn, and the SAFE loan instrument. Explains where EU defence money flows.
readings.tldr: Up to EUR 800 bn in EU defence money; SAFE loans favour European suppliers.

readings.title: Defence spending: who is doing what? (July 2026)
readings.summary: Country-by-country analysis of NATO's 2026 figures and the path to the Hague 3.5% + 1.5% target.
readings.tldr: Spending is rising everywhere, fastest on the eastern flank and in the Nordics.

readings.title: Russia's hybrid warfare campaign in Europe
readings.summary: Briefing on sabotage, cyberattacks, disinformation and drone incursions across Europe.
readings.tldr: Sabotage and drone incursions are the new normal, creating demand for protection of critical infrastructure.

readings.title: Ukraine Support Tracker
readings.summary: Tracks military, financial and humanitarian aid to Ukraine by country.
readings.tldr: Shows who funds Ukraine and how much, so you can see where the money is.

funding.title: Innovative public procurement (Innovative offentlige anskaffelser)

funding.tldr: Closes Monday 1 December at 13:00. Last chance to join a public buyer, Forsvaret included, as the supplier.

funding.title: Industrial PhD (Nærings-ph.d.)
funding.amount: NOK 145.8 m in total; 36–48 month projects
funding.who: Norwegian companies with a PhD candidate and a university partner
funding.tldr: Closes 7 December at 13:00. Tagged for defence and security; fund a PhD on your core tech.

funding.title: SkatteFUNN R&D tax deduction
funding.who: Norwegian companies with an R&D project
funding.tldr: Easiest non-dilutive money in Norway. Apply early; 1 September guarantees a same-year decision.

funding.title: Defence and security technology in the USA
funding.who: Norwegian defence and security tech companies
funding.tldr: Rolling intake for getting into the US defence market.

funding.title: NATO Innovation Fund
funding.tldr: A EUR 1 bn NATO-backed VC fund. Pitch any time.

funding.title: EDF application advice
funding.who: Norwegian companies preparing EU defence bids
funding.tldr: Free help to get ready for the 2027 EDF calls. Start now; consortia take months.

funding.title: PES: support to build EU and EDF applications
funding.amount: Up to NOK 500k per application (depends on role)
funding.who: Norwegian actors with a formal role in an EU or EDF application
funding.tldr: Get paid to write your EDF bid. Apply at least four weeks before the EU deadline.

funding.title: Centres for defence capability, security and preparedness
funding.amount: Up to NOK 450 m for 5–9 centres
funding.who: Only applicants who sent a sketch by 5 June 2026
funding.tldr: Main call deadline is planned for 20 January 2027. Only sketch applicants can lead; join a consortium now.

funding.title: NOK 1 bn Ukraine defence investment scheme
funding.amount: Fund investments, NOK 1 bn over 3 years
funding.who: Norwegian-based funds investing in Ukrainian defence companies
funding.tldr: Proposed November 2026. Norwegian–Ukrainian ventures should talk to fund managers now.

funding.title: Brave International
funding.who: Ukrainian and foreign companies; products tested in Ukraine
funding.tldr: Foreign firms can now win Brave1 grants. First joint calls not yet dated.

funding.title: Brave Norway
funding.who: Ukrainian and Norwegian defence startups (drones, AI)
funding.tldr: The Norway–Ukraine startup programme. Watch FFI and Brave1 for the next call.

funding.title: NATO DIANA challenge programme
funding.tldr: 2027 call closed 3 July 2026. Prepare now for the next call, usually mid-year.

funding.title: European Defence Fund (EDF) 2026 calls
funding.who: EU and EEA companies, Norway included
funding.tldr: 2026 calls closed 29 September. The 2027 work programme comes next.

funding.title: LINC: Launchpad for Innovative Norwegian Companies
funding.tldr: 2026 intake closed 20 April. Expect the next round in spring 2027.

tenders.title: Dynamic purchasing system: drone systems (RPAS)
tenders.tldr: Drone makers can apply to join at any time and then bid on Forsvaret's drone buys.

tenders.title: Dynamic purchasing system: ship technology services
tenders.tldr: Maritime tech and engineering firms can join any time to bid on ship-related jobs.

tenders.title: P1118 standardized vessels: prequalification
tenders.tldr: Yards bid; autonomy, sensor and C2 startups should team up with them now.

tenders.title: Digital learning platform for the defence sector (incl. AI content)
tenders.tldr: SaaS learning platform with AI for content and analysis. Fits training-tech startups.

tenders.title: Laboratory services for the Norwegian defence
tenders.tldr: Re-announced with a new deadline. Relevant for testing and lab companies.

tenders.title: Operation of Forsvaret's unclassified internet services
tenders.tldr: Hosting and operations incl. Azure. For IT and cloud operators.

tenders.title: Dynamic purchasing system: software licences
tenders.tldr: Software vendors and resellers can qualify any time to sell licences and subscriptions to the defence sector.

tenders.title: Visitor registration system for Forsvarsbygg
tenders.tldr: Self-service digital reception and visitor control, open to other defence agencies. Fits security software firms.

investors.name: Investinor

investors.note: Talk to them if you have a Ukrainian partner or JV.

investors.name: Gardar

investors.name: EIFO
